title: पत्रकार पक्राउ घटनाबारे मानव अधिकार आयोगले नेपाल प्रेससँग लियो विस्तृत जानकारी (भिडिओ)
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । समाचार कक्षबाटै पत्रकार पक्राउ गरेको घटनामा राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार आयोगले चासो लिएको छ । आज बिहान आयोगको टोली नेपाल प्रेस को कार्यालय आएर घटनाको विस्तृत जानकारी लिएको छ । आयोगका मानव अधिकार अधिकृत खिमानन्द बस्यालसहितको टोलीले स्थलगत अनुगमन गर्दै घटनाको विस्तृत विवरण लिएको हो । सो क्रममा पक्राउ परेका पत्रकार सुवेदीका साथै नेपाल प्रेसका अध्यक्ष विन्दुराज लम्साल, प्रधानसम्पादक मात्रिका पौडेल, सम्पादक चिरञ्जीवी पौडेलगायतले शुक्रबार साँझदेखि भएका घटनाक्रमबारे आयोगको टोलीलाई जानकारी गराएका थिए । प्रधानसम्पादक पौडेलले आफूहरूलाई साइबर ब्युरोमा करिब दुई घण्टा ह्यारेसमेन्ट गरिएको बताए । ‘समाचार कसले र किन लेखेको हो, यसको स्रोत को हो जस्ता प्रश्न गरेर केरकार गरियो । मेरो मोबाइल फोन समेत एक घण्टा नियन्त्रणमा लिइयो,’ पौडेलले भने । पौडेलले हाल नेपाली प्रेस अत्यन्तै असुरक्षित र त्रसित अवस्थामा रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै व्यक्तिगत गोपनीयता र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रतामाथि खुलेआम हस्तक्षेप तथा प्रहार भइरहेको बताए । ‘प्रेसको मुख थुन्न सकियो भने जे गरे पनि हुन्छ भन्ने खतरनाक प्रवृत्ति देखिँदैछ,’ उनले थपे, ‘पत्रकारलाई कसको निर्देशनमा र किन कार्यालयबाटै उठाइयो, त्यसबारे गहन अनुसन्धान हुनुपर्छ र भविष्यमा यस्ता घटना नदोहोरिने ग्यारेन्टी गरिनुपर्छ ।’ मानव अधिकार रक्षाको महत्वपूर्ण स्तम्भका रूपमा रहेको आयोगले गोपनीयताको हकको सुनिश्चितता र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको पक्षमा राज्यलाई आवश्यक दबाब दिनुपर्ने पौडेलले आग्रह गरे । छलफलपछि मानव अधिकार अधिकृत बस्यालले पत्रकार पक्राउको विषयलाई आयोगले नजिकबाट र गम्भीरतापूर्वक नियालिरहेको बताए । उनले यसबारे आयोगले छिट्टै आफ्नो आधिकारिक धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्ने जानकारी दिए । साथै, घटनाको थप अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक परे पत्रकारलाई पक्राउको आदेश दिने प्रहरी तथा सरकारी अधिकृतहरूसँग समेत बयान लिइने बस्यालले स्पष्ट पारे । गत शुक्रबार साँझ नेपाल प्रेसको कार्यालयबाटै पत्रकार सुवेदीलाई प्रहरीले नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो। Kathmandu. A team from the National Human Rights Commission has arrived at the Nepal Press office to investigate the incident of the arrest of journalists from the newsroom. A team led by the Commission's Human Rights Officer Khimananda Basyal conducted on-site monitoring and took detailed details of the incident. During the course of the investigation, arrested journalist Subedi, as well as Nepal Press Chairman Bindu Raj Lamsal, Editor-in-Chief Matrika Poudel, Editor Chiranjivi Poudel, and others informed the Commission team about the events that had taken place since Friday evening. Editor-in-Chief Poudel said that they were harassed for about two hours at the Cyber Bureau. "They interrogated me by asking questions like who wrote the news and why, and who the source was. My mobile phone was also taken away for an hour," Poudel said. Poudel said that the Nepali press is currently in a very unsafe and panicked state, and that personal privacy and press freedom are being openly interfered with and attacked. "There is a dangerous trend that if the press can be silenced, anything will do," he added. "There should be a thorough investigation into who ordered the journalist to be removed from office and why, and guarantees should be made that such incidents do not recur in the future." Poudel urged that the commission, which is an important pillar of human rights protection, should exert necessary pressure on the state to ensure the right to privacy and press freedom. After the discussion, Human Rights Officer Basyal said that the commission is closely and seriously monitoring the issue of the journalist's arrest. He informed that the commission will soon make its official position public on the matter. Also, Basyal clarified that if necessary, statements will be taken from the police and government officials who ordered the journalist's arrest for further investigation into the incident. Police took journalist Subedi into custody from the Nepal Press office last Friday evening.

A team from the National Human Rights Commission has arrived at the Nepal Press office to investigate the incident of the arrest of journalists from the newsroom. A team led by the Commission's Human Rights Officer Khimananda Basyal conducted on-site monitoring and took detailed details of the incident. During the course of the investigation, arrested journalist Subedi, as well as Nepal Press Chairman Bindu Raj Lamsal, Editor-in-Chief Matrika Poudel, Editor Chiranjivi Poudel, and others informed the Commission team about the events that had taken place since Friday evening. Editor-in-Chief Poudel said that they were harassed for about two hours at the Cyber Bureau. "They interrogated me by asking questions like who wrote the news and why, and who the source was. My mobile phone was also taken away for an hour," Poudel said. Poudel said that the Nepali press is currently in a very unsafe and panicked state, and that personal privacy and press freedom are being openly interfered with and attacked. "There is a dangerous trend that if the press can be silenced, anything will do," he added. "There should be a thorough investigation into who ordered the journalist to be removed from office and why, and guarantees should be made that such incidents do not recur in the future." Poudel urged that the commission, which is an important pillar of human rights protection, should exert necessary pressure on the state to ensure the right to privacy and press freedom. After the discussion, Human Rights Officer Basyal said that the commission is closely and seriously monitoring the issue of the journalist's arrest. He informed that the commission will soon make its official position public on the matter. Also, Basyal clarified that if necessary, statements will be taken from the police and government officials who ordered the journalist's arrest for further investigation into the incident. Police took journalist Subedi into custody from the Nepal Press office last Friday evening.

गत शुक्रबार साँझ नेपाल प्रेसको कार्यालयबाटै पत्रकार सुवेदीलाई प्रहरीले नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो।

Kathmandu. A team from the National Human Rights Commission has arrived at the Nepal Press office to investigate the incident of the arrest of journalists from the newsroom. A team led by the Commission's Human Rights Officer Khimananda Basyal conducted on-site monitoring and took detailed details of the incident. During the course of the investigation, arrested journalist Subedi, as well as Nepal Press Chairman Bindu Raj Lamsal, Editor-in-Chief Matrika Poudel, Editor Chiranjivi Poudel, and others informed the Commission team about the events that had taken place since Friday evening. Editor-in-Chief Poudel said that they were harassed for about two hours at the Cyber Bureau. "They interrogated me by asking questions like who wrote the news and why, and who the source was. My mobile phone was also taken away for an hour," Poudel said. Poudel said that the Nepali press is currently in a very unsafe and panicked state, and that personal privacy and press freedom are being openly interfered with and attacked. "There is a dangerous trend that if the press can be silenced, anything will do," he added. "There should be a thorough investigation into who ordered the journalist to be removed from office and why, and guarantees should be made that such incidents do not recur in the future." Poudel urged that the commission, which is an important pillar of human rights protection, should exert necessary pressure on the state to ensure the right to privacy and press freedom. After the discussion, Human Rights Officer Basyal said that the commission is closely and seriously monitoring the issue of the journalist's arrest. He informed that the commission will soon make its official position public on the matter. Also, Basyal clarified that if necessary, statements will be taken from the police and government officials who ordered the journalist's arrest for further investigation into the incident. Police took journalist Subedi into custody from the Nepal Press office last Friday evening.
